summary: Robert Henry Lawson Slater was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his M.A. from Cambridge and Ph.D. from Columbia. He held posts at the University of Rangoon, Huron University College, McGill, and Harvard.
Robert Hinde studied at St John's College and Balliol College, Oxford, and taught John Hurrell Crook. He spent his career at the University of Cambridge from circa 1950 to 1994.

Robert Hunter was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Aberdeen, Marischal College, and the University of Edinburgh. He served as a missionary with the Free Church of Scotland Mission from 1846 to 1855.

Robert I. Crane was an historian and Indologist who studied at Duke and Yale. He held academic posts at the University of Chicago, University of Michigan, Duke University, and served as Ford-Maxwell Professor at Syracuse University from 1968 to 1990.

Robert Isaac Levy was an Indologist and anthropologist who held a post at Duke University. He served as Professor of Anthropology at UC San Diego (1969-1991) and as Research Professor at UNC Chapel Hill (circa 1990-2003).

Robert J. Miller, a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies, earned his B.A. at Michigan and Ph.D. at Washington. He held posts at the University of Washington, the American Institute of Indian Studies, and Wisconsin-Madison (1959-1988).
Robert J. Topmiller worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Kentucky under the supervision of George C. Herring.

Robert Kritzer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held posts at UC Berkeley and Kyoto Notre Dame University, where he taught Achim Bayer.
Robert Kyd studied at the University of Edinburgh and founded the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden in 1787.

Robert L. Brown worked in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a curator at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (circa 1980-2014) and Professor Emeritus at the University of California, Los Angeles (circa 1985-2014).

Robert Lenz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tartu and earned his Dr. Ph. under Franz Bopp in Berlin. He taught at Tallinn Cathedral School and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University.
Robert Lingat was an Indologist and historian who earned his doctorate from the University of Paris. He taught law at Thammasat, Indochina, and Saigon, and held positions at the EPHE and INALCO.

Robert M. Gimello was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Columbia University. He taught at the University of Arizona from circa 1981 to 2020 and served as a professor at Harvard University.

Robert Maclagan was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering. He served as Principal of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (1847-1860).

Robert Magliola is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from Princeton. He held positions at Purdue, Tamkang University, Assumption University of Thailand, National Taiwan University, and Columbia University.

Robert Mason Towers was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Trinity College Dublin. He served as Professor of Bengali at King's College London and as a University Teacher at the University of Cambridge.

Robert Mayer, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at Bristol and Leiden under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen. In 2002, he was a member of the Oriental Studies Faculty at Oxford.
Robert Needham Cust was an Indologist and linguist educated at Eton, Cambridge, Haileybury, and Edinburgh. He served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1843 to 1867.
Robert Orme was an historian and Indologist who attended Harrow School and served as Historiographer for the East India Company from 1769 to 1801.

Robert P. Goldman is an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Pennsylvania, studying under Ludo Rocher and Shivram Dattatray Joshi. He spent his academic career at UC Berkeley, where he became Professor in 1983 and later Professor Emeritus.
